title: Trace Synthesis Workload Catalog and Regression Playlist
body:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog of synthetic workload scenarios derived from production traces, plus a short regression "playlist" (priority order of microbench steps) for quickly reproducing perf regressions. The goal is to standardize inputs for kernel/scheduler/kv-cache experiments so bench runs are comparable across engineers and CI lanes.

Scope and motivation:
- We frequently see flaky perf changes due to small kernel changes, scheduler tweaks, or KV cache invalidation behavior. Having canonical synthesized traces that exercise specific micro-paths (short prefix reuse, long KV-eviction churn, dense attention vs sparse tokens, varied batch-deltas) reduces debugging time.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: scenarios are small, reproducible, and parameterizable. Not every scenario mirrors full-prod traffic; instead they isolate subsystems.

High-level harness architecture (notes):
- Core components: trace-synth engine (python), workload-driver (go), local-run harness (docker-compose for dev), CI lane (k8s job).
- Input format: sequence of request events (arrival_ts_ms, model, prompt_hash, key_prefix_id, seq_len, sampling_params). We keep the format CSV-like for ease of diffs.
- Outputs: per-request latency, per-token time breakdown (attention, kernel exec, scheduler-batch-wait, kv-lookup), kernel-call-counts, GPU occupancy summary (sampled), memory high-water marks.
- Observability hooks: spans injected into harness and translated to our tracing schema (trace_id -> span events) so microtrace replay can map to production traces.

Scenario catalog (each scenario is ~30-120s depending on scale):
1) Short-prefix reuse (S-PREFIX-1): many small requests (seq_len 32) with identical first-8 tokens across a 60s window to exercise prefix KV hits and prefix-merge fast path. Params: QPS 200, batch max 32, kv_cache_ttl=5m. Expected to show high KV hit rate and low per-token kernel exec.
2) Long-eviction churn (EVICT-LOOP-2): high variety prompts that force constant KV insert+evict cycles. Params: QPS 50, unique_prefixes_per_min 5000, kv_capacity small (simulated 4k entries), batch max 16. Useful for testing eviction heuristics and mem copies.
3) Heterogeneous-batches (HETER-3): mixed seq lengths (16/64/512) arriving in patterns to stress continuous batching and scheduler heuristics. Pattern: 70% short, 20% mid, 10% long. Evaluate batch packing penalties and kernel fallback costs.
4) Kernel-stress-quant (KERNEL-QUANT-4): synthetic tokens that force quantized kernels with different alignment (non-multiple-of-8 channels) to catch slow paths in low-precision kernels. Single GPU at QPS 30, repeat for various channel widths.
5) Cold-kv-warmup (COLD-WARM-5): start with empty cache and ramp QPS from 0 -> 300 over 3 minutes to measure warm-up spike and cache population latency.
6) Tooling-edge-cases (TOOLING-6): includes malformed requests, slight param variance, and frequent fallback model switches to ensure robust tracing and failover telemetry.

Metric definitions (what we measure):
- p50/p95/p99 request latency (ms) end-to-end
- per-token median kernel exec time (ms)
- scheduler-wait time breakdown (ms): time spent waiting for batch, serialization overhead, inter-op queue waits
- kv-hit-rate (by prefix length), kv-eviction-rate (% of insertions that trigger evict), kv-copy-bytes
- batch-utilization (avg batch size / max batch size)
- GPU occupancy: sampled SM utilization and mem bw (approx)
- regression score: a synthetic single-number combining 99th latency and kv-eviction spikes (used for alerting in CI)

Synthesis method (how traces are derived from prod traces):
- Step 1: extract anonymized sequence features from prod traces (prefix hashes, seq_len distribution, inter-arrival delta distribution per route).
- Step 2: cluster sessions by heavy hitters (top 100 prefixes) and tail patterns (long seq tail).
- Step 3: generate parametric workload descriptions (CSV). Add random jitter between inter-arrival times to avoid lockstep.
- Step 4: validate: run 3x short replay in sandbox and compare feature distributions to source traces (KL divergence thresholds).

Recent microbench runs (sample notes, dev runs on dev-gpu-4):
- 2026-02-25: Ran S-PREFIX-1 against kernel-merge-opt branch. Observed 7% p95 regression vs baseline. Per-span breakdown shows increased scheduler-batch-wait (median +6ms) despite lower kernel exec. Suspect change to packer logic introduced serialization that prevented opportunistic merging. Logged PR #842.
- 2026-02-28: EVICT-LOOP-2 run with kv-lru-fix reverted — eviction-rate dropped but memory copies increased 12% (copy bandwidth spike). Root cause: copying semantics moved to slow path in commit a1b2c (see PR).
- 2026-03-03: HETER-3 exposes degenerate batch composition where long-seq requests hold batch slots for 800ms and block short samples; temp mitigation: add short-request priority lane in scheduler (config flag: scheduler.short_priority=true) — reduced p99 by 18% in smoke runs.

Regression playlist (ordered reproduce steps):
A) Reproduce S-PREFIX-1 p95 regression locally: check out runtime@merge-opt-pr842, run harness with --scenario S-PREFIX-1 --seed 42 --collect-spans. Attach output to PR.
B) Run kernel micro-tests: run kernel bench binary with alignment patterns used by KERNEL-QUANT-4; assert no slow path triggered.
C) EVICT-LOOP-2 mem-profiling: run scenario under nvprof and capture memcpy histogram. If memcpy > baseline by 10%, block further rollouts.
D) HETER-3 scheduler trace: enable verbose scheduler tracing and produce flame graph; confirm whether long requests are occupying batching windows for >500ms.

Playbook & quick checklist (for oncall/dev):
- If CI flags regression score > threshold:
  - Run regression playlist A-D on the failing commit.
  - If reproduction successful, post short debug summary to #eng-serving-runtime and tag authors.
  - Create Jira with minimal repro steps + attached harness output.
- Oncall quick commands (devbox shortcuts):
  - ./harness/run.sh --scenario S-PREFIX-1 --ci-mode --upload-artifact 
  - tools/microbench/kernel_bench --pattern=odd-channels --iters=1000
  - python tools/kv_inspect.py --run=EVICT-LOOP-2 --output=evict.hist

Open questions / TODOs:
- Formalize thresholding rules for regression score and add to CI gating. (TODO: draft proposal, owner: Aisha)
notes: This is a working draft intended for eng-serving-runtime reviewers. Contains TODOs and commands that reference internal dev tooling. Please point out missing scenarios or parameter suggestions.
